title: The fight over the Siang dam
dek: Villages along the Siang oppose an 11,000 MW dam that would submerge 27 villages. Four villagers have been detained under an anti-terror law, and gatherings are banned.

photos.alt: A wide, calm river between forested hills, with tall grass in the foreground.
photos.caption: The Siang river in Arunachal Pradesh. The proposed Siang Upper Multipurpose Project would dam this river.

photos.caption: Nugong Bridge, where the Siang meets the Siyom river.

photos.caption: The Siang river and its rocky banks in Arunachal Pradesh.

story.text: The Siang Upper Multipurpose Project is an 11,000 MW hydropower plant being developed by NHPC. Mongabay India reports it would submerge 27 villages, including Yingkiong, Upper Siang's district headquarters, and residents of Siang, Upper Siang and East Siang districts have consistently opposed it.

The current protests oppose a pre-feasibility study by NHPC at the proposed dam sites, one of the last studies before the dam's detailed project report. Early this month protests turned violent: protesters set fire to vehicles and stormed an MLA's house, and police allegedly lathi-charged protesters on 4 October.

On 9 October four villagers of Geku, Adum Tayom, Omak Paron, Okut Paloh and Oson Paron, were detained under the Arunachal Pradesh Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 2014. Their lawyer says the families at first received only notices, not the detention orders. On 11 October the district banned gatherings of five or more people.

On 14 October a sessions court in East Siang gave 13 people named in two police cases interim protection from arrest, pending further hearings. Local groups have asked for the detainees' release, the withdrawal of central armed police and a halt to the dam studies.

official.text: The district magistrate's detention orders cite a tense and volatile situation, violence and arson, and say the detentions are meant to contain unlawful activities and protect public safety. Upper Siang's District Collector told Mongabay India the area was peaceful and that detainees must make representations to the state government.
